diagrams.title: Build Evidence, Sell Support, Separate Award Exposure
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages from lawful public signals to paid counsel work
diagrams.assumptions_note: Public anomalies are research leads rather than established violations. Retainers pay for defined analytical services. An analyst does not acquire statutory claimant eligibility merely by preparing a dossier for someone else.
diagrams.caption: Use Python sqlite3, hashlib, and csv for reproducible research; preserve source provenance before transforming records. Only licensed relator counsel files an FCA complaint under 31 U.S.C. § 3730(b)(2). Route SEC Form TCR and IRS Form 211 submissions through counsel as an operating requirement.

stages.label: Acquire Lawful Records
stages.value: Step 1: document source and access authority
stages.detail: Collect CMS Part B/D, Open Payments, SAM.gov, and lawfully obtained import-manifest records. Record publication dates, source URLs, permitted uses, and SHA-256 hashes; exclude improperly acquired records.

stages.label: Rank Explainable Signals
stages.detail: Normalize specialties, geography, utilization, coding changes, contract modifications, and shipment units. Use peer-adjusted comparisons and negative controls; an outlier without context is not a fraud conclusion.

stages.label: Corroborate Claim Elements
stages.value: Step 3: tie allegations to primary evidence
stages.detail: Build a claim ledger linking dates, actors, amounts, government payment requests, and supporting records. Track FOIA provenance and disclosure history; public FOIA material can affect public-disclosure analysis.

stages.label: Contract Counsel Support
stages.detail: Use paid scopes for reproducible notebooks, claim reconstruction, exhibits, and ongoing analytical support. Invoice service milestones independently of litigation outcomes and preserve conflict checks.

stages.label: Segregate Contingent Outcomes
stages.value: Step 5: restrict sealed materials and award ledgers
stages.detail: Counsel controls filing, service, court orders, and permitted disclosure. Maintain least-privilege matter workspaces. Carry potential awards at zero in operating cash budgets until actual eligible proceeds arrive.

diagrams.title: A Screening Funnel, Not an Award Forecast
diagrams.subtitle: Nested illustrative cohorts end in paid firm-matter engagements
diagrams.assumptions_note: Synthetic mature-year cohort, not measured conversion history. All stages count distinct firm-matter opportunities, each anchored to an initial signal; later stages are subsets of earlier stages. Five engagements belong to five separate firms. No conversion stage represents an agency recovery probability.
diagrams.caption: Sequential conversion is 18.0%, 33.3%, 30.0%, and 27.8%; overall conversion is 0.5%. Annual engagement fees of $60,000, $75,000, $90,000, $112,500, and $150,000 total $487,500. This is a mature annual service model, not a 30-day sales promise; first deal timing is 4–12 months.

stages.label: Screened Opportunities
stages.detail: Deduplicate related entities and repeated anomalies before counting opportunities. Record one candidate firm and one traceable matter hypothesis per entry.

stages.label: Corroborated Opportunities
stages.detail: Retain only opportunities with independent corroboration and a plausible payment, securities, or tax nexus. Reject stale identifiers and ordinary coding variation.

stages.label: Counsel-Screened Opportunities
stages.detail: Counsel assesses conflicts, public disclosure, source eligibility, and evidence specificity. This screen does not establish liability or entitlement to payment.

stages.label: Scoped Support Proposals
stages.detail: Prepare priced analytical scopes with acceptance criteria, lawful access boundaries, named deliverables, payment schedules, and segregated matter permissions.

stages.label: Paid Retainer Engagements
stages.detail: Execute five distinct annual service engagements. Track invoices and collections separately from contingent filings; no award proceeds fund payroll.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $487,500 Revenue to $219,375 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical 45.0% annual net margin
diagrams.assumptions_note: Formula v2.0 scenario totals are fixed; expense categories below are an illustrative reconciliation rather than supplied historical accounts. Base revenue is entirely earned B2B service fees, with $0 contingent awards. Positive endpoints are totals; the four negative bars are expense movements. Do not add the final total to the preceding movements.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $95,000 revenue less $64,600 costs equals $30,400 owner profit at 32%, with 1 FT + 2 C. Base: $487,500 less $268,125 equals $219,375 at 45.0%, with 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled: $880,000 less $369,600 equals $510,400 at 58%, with 2 FT + 3 C. All three scenarios can be modeled with zero award receipts. Government recoveries, sanctions, tax proceeds, and client funds are not operator revenue.

stages.label: Recognized Service Revenue
stages.detail: Five annual engagements supply the opening total. Recognize services as earned and track cash collection separately. Exclude agency recoveries and uncollected claims; recognize only the operator's eligible retained portion of any separately realized award.

stages.label: Delivery Labor
stages.detail: Illustrative allocation covers contracted analytical delivery and non-owner delivery support. Residual owner profit is owner compensation, not an additional salary deduction; remaining contribution is $322,500.

stages.label: Evidence Infrastructure
stages.value: Subtract $36,000 annual data and tooling expense
stages.detail: Budget licensed datasets, secure matter storage, reproducible processing, backup retention, and source retrieval. Record subscription rights by project; remaining contribution is $286,500.

stages.label: Specialist Matter Support
stages.detail: Budget business-side specialist consultation and external technical validation. Do not imply that this purchases representation for every relator; remaining contribution is $244,500.

stages.label: Operating Overhead
stages.detail: Allocate insurance, bookkeeping, secure communications, business development, and administration. Total deductions reach $268,125, leaving $219,375.

stages.label: Annual Owner Profit
stages.detail: Closing total equals $487,500 minus $268,125. Non-delivery operating categories total $103,125 annually, or $8,593.75 monthly, within the stated $1,500–$9,500 operating range; total costs including delivery labor average $22,343.75 monthly.

diagrams.title: Five Paid Research Niches Fund the Base Case
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative annual service-fee yield per distinct firm engagement
diagrams.assumptions_note: Bars represent annual operator service revenue in USD, not statutory award percentages, expected recoveries, or empirical market prices. Each niche contributes one distinct engagement to the five-engagement Base model; total revenue is $487,500.
diagrams.caption: Price around reproducible evidence work and counsel demand. A payment rail determines the research problem, not automatic award eligibility. Invoice support services independently of whether counsel files a complaint or an agency takes action.

stages.label: CMS Part B/D Support
stages.detail: Reconcile provider identifiers, billing periods, specialty cohorts, and payment records. Aggregate utilization anomalies require claim-level corroboration before supporting a particularized FCA allegation.

stages.label: Open Payments Corroboration
stages.detail: Resolve manufacturer, recipient, and payment identities against relevant utilization records. A disclosed payment does not itself prove an unlawful inducement or a resulting false reimbursement claim.

stages.label: Procurement and Customs
stages.detail: Link procurement representations and authorized shipment evidence to specific contracts or entries. Test alternative explanations including amendments, valuation methods, timing, and entity mismatches.

stages.label: SEC Evidence Analytics
stages.detail: Provide issuer-event reconstruction and original-analysis support. Counsel evaluates 15 U.S.C. § 78u-6 and 17 CFR § 240.21F-4; SEC award percentages generally run 10%–30%, not the FCA intervention schedule.

stages.label: IRS Evidence Analytics
stages.detail: Reconcile lawful records to tax periods and asserted underpayments. Counsel tests 26 U.S.C. § 7623(b), including amounts exceeding $2 million and, for individual taxpayers, gross income exceeding $200,000 in a qualifying taxable year.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before a Filing Strategy
diagrams.subtitle: Separate source eligibility, claim detail, procedure, and recovery risk
diagrams.assumptions_note: The renderer presents four sequential decision nodes; each detail states its proceed or stop branch. Numerical recovery parameters are sensitivity assumptions, not observed DOJ intervention or Granston-era dismissal rates. Agency and court outcomes require matter-specific assessment.
diagrams.caption: FCA shares generally run 15%–25% after government intervention and 25%–30% without intervention, subject to statutory exceptions and reductions. SEC and CFTC generally use 10%–30%; IRS § 7623(b) generally uses 15%–30%. No common 15%–30% rate should be applied across programs. Annual operating cash includes zero pending award value.

stages.label: Source Eligibility
stages.value: Check 1: proceed only with defensible eligibility
stages.detail: For FCA matters, counsel tests 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), qualifying public disclosures, and original-source requirements; public-data mining alone does not bypass the bar. If unresolved, stop filing preparation and resolve the issue. Separately test SEC or IRS eligibility under its own rules.

stages.label: Claim Particularity
stages.value: Check 2: proceed with adequately supported allegations
stages.detail: Counsel tests Rule 9(b), applicable circuit standards, and 31 U.S.C. § 3729 elements. Build representative claim links where required: who, what, when, where, amount, payment request, and evidence. If specificity fails, obtain lawful corroboration or stop.

stages.label: Seal and Submission Control
stages.value: Check 3: proceed only through controlled counsel procedure
stages.detail: FCA complaints remain sealed for at least 60 days under § 3730(b)(2), with court-authorized extensions. Do not serve the defendant before court direction. Seal breaches can cause sanctions or dismissal, but dismissal is not automatic. Restrict access; route SEC TCR and IRS 211 separately through counsel.

stages.label: Zero-Recovery Stress Test
stages.value: Check 4: fund operations without pending recoveries
stages.detail: Illustrative FCA sensitivity uses intervention i=20%, non-intervention=80%, dismissal conditional on non-intervention d=25%, and positive collection probabilities of 60% after intervention and 20% after non-intervention survival. Collection probability is i*0.60+(1-i)*(1-d)*0.20=24%; zero collection is 76%. A severe case with both collection probabilities at zero yields zero recovery. Model government dismissal, including Granston-policy risk, under § 3730(c)(2)(A); non-intervention itself is not dismissal. Exclude all pending amounts from operating cash regardless of modeled probability.

diagrams.title: Three Core People, Five at Scale
diagrams.subtitle: Core 1 FT + 2 C becomes 2 FT + 3 C without counting client counsel
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT denotes a full-time seat; C denotes a contractor seat, not a full-time equivalent. Numeric value is one person per seat. The first three seats form the core pod; the final two activate only in the Scaled scenario. Client counsel is an external relationship, not an uncounted pod employee.
diagrams.caption: Core staffing supports the $95,000 Conservative and $487,500 Base revenue scenarios. Five-person staffing supports the $880,000 Scaled scenario. Access follows assigned matters rather than seniority; client counsel retains filing and legal-strategy responsibility.

stages.label: Core Owner Operator
stages.detail: Own client acquisition, engagement scope, billing, delivery acceptance, and cash reserves. Separate service invoices from contingent-award tracking and escalate legal questions to retained counsel.

stages.label: Core Data Engineer
stages.detail: Build lawful ingestion, identifier resolution, versioned transformations, hashing, and reproducible anomaly rankings. Maintain source-to-exhibit lineage and restrict access to assigned client matters.

stages.label: Core Forensic Analyst
stages.detail: Corroborate anomalies, maintain claim ledgers, test benign explanations, and prepare evidence indexes. Track conflicting facts rather than excluding records that weaken the working hypothesis.

stages.label: Scaled Delivery Lead
stages.detail: Coordinate parallel engagements, document acceptance criteria, monitor service capacity, and audit source lineage. Activate only when contracted service revenue supports recurring delivery commitments.

stages.label: Scaled Specialist Analyst
stages.detail: Add healthcare coding, securities, customs, or tax expertise against defined paid scopes. Limit specialist access to relevant records and record technical assumptions in each delivered exhibit.

diagrams.title: Allocate $30,000 Before Expanding the Pod
diagrams.subtitle: Four capital buckets inside the $10,000–$45,000 startup range
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values represent a $30,000 central startup plan. Each detail supplies matching lean and expanded allocations: lean totals $10,000; expanded totals $45,000. Startup capital is not additional recognized revenue or an automatic annual expense. Reserve balances become expenses only when spent on qualifying operating costs.
diagrams.caption: Central allocation is $8,000 + $7,000 + $5,000 + $10,000 = $30,000. Monthly operating needs span $1,500–$9,500; a $10,000 cash reserve covers only about 1.1–6.7 months before delivery labor and other excluded commitments. With first deals taking 4–12 months, stage spending and secure additional runway rather than anticipating awards.

stages.label: Lawful Evidence Access
stages.detail: Lean allocation is $2,000; expanded allocation is $12,000. Purchase necessary dataset rights, limited source retrieval, and targeted corroboration rather than broad subscriptions without paid demand.

stages.label: Secure Research Environment
stages.detail: Lean allocation is $2,000; expanded allocation is $10,000. Fund encrypted endpoints, matter-level permissions, backups, reproducible processing, and access logging before sensitive materials arrive.

stages.label: Engagement and Quality Setup
stages.detail: Lean allocation is $2,000; expanded allocation is $8,000. Fund engagement documentation, initial insurance costs, external technical checks, and counsel-directed handling procedures for sensitive work.

stages.label: Uncommitted Cash Reserve
stages.detail: Lean allocation is $4,000; expanded allocation is $15,000. Keep liquidity available for delayed collections and essential operating costs; do not treat sealed matters as cash collateral.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Counsel-Ready Research Operation
diagrams.subtitle: Build a defensible paid-support capability, not a rushed complaint
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone end days. This sprint establishes operating readiness; it does not shorten the 4–12 month first-deal window or the illustrative 2–5+ year award horizon. FCA investigations may remain under extended seal for years; SEC and IRS submissions do not use the FCA complaint-seal procedure.
diagrams.caption: Exit the sprint with one reproducible research package, a counsel-reviewed service scope, and a collection-aware cash plan. Recurring support revenue funds operations. Model every pending award as zero cash and stress a permanent zero-recovery outcome before adding fixed costs.

stages.label: Days 1–7
stages.value: Milestone 1: establish scope and source controls
stages.detail: Choose one niche and define a lawful data inventory. Create source hashes, access permissions, entity resolution rules, and a register of disclosure dates. Draft specific analytical service deliverables.

stages.label: Days 8–14
stages.value: Milestone 2: reproduce and challenge one signal
stages.detail: Build a small SQLite evidence store and deterministic transforms. Test one anomaly against matched peers and benign explanations. Preserve failed hypotheses and document missing claim-level evidence.

stages.label: Days 15–21
stages.detail: Arrange confidential counsel assessment of conflicts, public disclosure, eligibility, particularity, and handling restrictions. Define paid support scope; do not circulate sealed or restricted material as a marketing sample.

stages.label: Days 22–30
stages.value: Milestone 4: prepare delivery and cash controls
stages.detail: Finalize exhibit lineage, acceptance criteria, invoice milestones, and access logs. Build a 13-week cash forecast with zero award receipts and delayed retainer collections. Scale outreach using sanitized methods demonstrations, not allegations.
